content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model overestimates prices during sharp upward moves, then fails to correct downward after peaks.
- Model shows persistent lag in responding to recent price drops — forecasts remain too high longer than actuals.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured; model holds onto high forecasts too long after peaks.
- Forecasts tend to be overly optimistic in the first 5–10 days of the horizon, especially when history shows strong upward momentum.
- Model underreacts to sustained downward trends; forecasts remain elevated even when true prices are falling.
- When true prices spike, model forecasts overshoot and then fail to adjust — creating a “peak overshoot” bias.
- Model exhibits strong bias toward recent low prices, underweighting recent high prices in forecasting.
- Forecasts are more accurate when the 30-day history includes recent volatility — model performs worse when history is flat or trending down.
